messages:
maria: Billing asked: how do we tag requests when we fallback to a lower plan? they want cost attribution for bursts & fallbacks.

kevin: Clarify: are we talking about per-org rollbacks (when org hits quota) vs per-key throttles? different telemetry needs.

maria: Good point — both. Billing needs to see 'billed_plan' (what they were charged), 'serving_plan' (what actually ran), and 'enforcement_reason' (softcap|hardcap|fallback|routing).

sam: Proposal: add three labels on every request event: metering.plan.primary, metering.plan.effective, metering.enforcement.reason

rachel: +1. Also expose a dashboard row that shows volume split by primary vs effective plan so finance can reconcile.

kevin: Implementation detail: priority lookup should be: org_assigned_plan -> key_override_plan -> usage_promoted_plan -> default_free

maria: Example mapping snippet:
```
priority:
  - org_plan
  - api_key_plan
  - promoted_plan
  - free
```
If effective != primary, emit metering.enforcement.reason=promoted|demoted|fallback

ops-bot: rate-limiter v2 applied softcap to org:org_42, reason=burst_control, window=60s

anne: UX note — console should show the 'effective plan' (hover: why demoted) and support exporting CSV with those metering labels.

sam: Telemetry: tag traces with metering.* and add a low-cardinality 'enforcement_bucket' for aggregation. Don't use high-cardinality strings.

rachel: For billing reconciliation, we also need a 'fallback_multiplier' field when we route to cheaper model (e.g., quantized) so cost reports can apply different unit rates.

maria: Action items: kevin/prio rules + sam/telemetry schema + anne/console mockups. I'll sync with billing next Wed.

kevin: I'll open a tiny RFC with the lookup LUT and example events. thx.

maria: Thanks :thumbsup:
